chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the man who gets thirsty in the month of Ramadan, he (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem if he were to suck the ring.
ai.seo_question: Does sucking a ring break the fast in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the principle of *al-istihlak* (consumption) in Shia jurisprudence, where ingesting a small amount of a non-food item to relieve thirst does not break the fast. It highlights the practical leniency granted to the fasting individual, distinguishing between mere sucking for relief and actual consumption of a substantial quantity.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
regarding the man who gets thirsty in the Month of Ramaan. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem if he were to suck the ring’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who becomes thirsty in the month of Ramadan.
He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful if he sucks his signet.’”
